links.outcome: Readability grade level of ChatGPT and website brain tumor prognosis materials
links.effect: Zero websites and ChatGPT responses met 6th or 8th grade benchmarks; 93.3% of ChatGPT responses were graduate level; ChatGPT less readable than websites across all metrics (p<0.001).
links.quote: Among ChatGPT responses, 93.3 % were graduate level.

links.outcome: Reading level of patient materials versus AMA/NIH recommended grade levels
links.effect: Zero websites and ChatGPT responses met the 6th grade or below (AMA) or 8th grade or below (NIH) benchmarks; 50.4% of websites at 9th-12th grade, 47.9% undergraduate, 1.7% graduate.
links.quote: Zero websites and ChatGPT responses met the readability benchmarks of 6th grade or below (AMA guideline) or 8th grade or below (NIH guideline).

unlisted_practices: Professional medical review of online patient education materials associated with better readability (higher FRE, lower CLI)

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation measuring the readability of ChatGPT-generated patient education materials compared to online websites using standard readability formulas; does not test a specific deployment safeguard or intervention.
